# PLAN — iteration 1

## Current state assessment

The baseline passes simulation and has 12 LUTs and 4 FFs, but routed setup fails at WNS −0.753 ns on the `read_ptr` → LUTRAM read → `out_data[7]` path; hold passes at WHS +0.109 ns. Timing recovery is the first gate, so prioritize removing that output read path while preserving the one-cycle minimum transfer age, two-entry capacity, handshakes, reset behavior, and full throughput. The eventual objective remains minimizing LUTs.

## Hypothesis

Replacing the indexed LUTRAM output with a head data register that directly drives `out_data` should reduce the output path delay and may close setup timing, at the cost of additional FFs for the two stored words.

## Instruction for generator

In `skid_buffer_core`, replace the `storage[read_ptr]` indexed output with explicit 8-bit head and tail registers, and drive `out_data` directly from the head register; update them on push/pop combinations so the oldest word remains at the head, including simultaneous push/pop when full. Preserve the exact occupancy-based `in_ready` and `out_valid` behavior, synchronous active-high reset, stalled payload stability, and one-cycle minimum transfer age; leave data unspecified when `out_valid` is low. Keep the top module interface and its `// @latency 1` annotation unchanged.
